root_cause.text: In `mtk_xdp_setup()` of the MediaTek Ethernet driver, the XDP/eBPF program pointer `eth->prog` was replaced and the old program later released before rollback on `mtk_open()` failure, leaving the driver with an incorrect program pointer and refcount state on setup error.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an error path after `old_prog = rcu_replace_pointer(eth->prog, prog, ...)` that, if `mtk_open(dev)` fails, restores `eth->prog` with `rcu_assign_pointer(eth->prog, old_prog)` and returns immediately; the commit message explicitly says to “Reset eBPF program pointer to old_prog and do not decrease its ref-count if mtk_open routine in mtk_xdp_setup() fails.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In `mtk_xdp_setup()` of the MediaTek Ethernet driver, the XDP/eBPF program pointer `eth->prog` was replaced and the old program later released before rollback on `mtk_open()` failure, leaving the driver with an incorrect program pointer and refcount state on setup error.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds an error path after `old_prog = rcu_replace_pointer(eth->prog, prog, ...)` that, if `mtk_open(dev)` fails, restores `eth->prog` with `rcu_assign_pointer(eth->prog, old_prog)` and returns immediately; the commit message explicitly says to “Reset eBPF program pointer to old_prog and do not decrease its ref-count if mtk_open routine in mtk_xdp_setup() fails.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Rollback the XDP program pointer if device reopen fails during setup so XDP updates are not left partially applied.
intent_record.what: The code moves the conditional device restart logic to immediately after `rcu_replace_pointer(eth->prog, prog, ...)`, expands the `if (netif_running(dev) && need_update)` block to call `mtk_open(dev)` into a local `err` variable, and adds an error path that restores `eth->prog` back to `old_prog` with `rcu_assign_pointer()` before returning the open failure; the old trailing `return mtk_open(dev);` statement is removed.
intent_record.how: When the device is running and an update requires reopening, the function now rolls back the XDP program pointer if `mtk_open()` fails instead of leaving the new program installed while the reopen operation fails. This keeps the driver state consistent and avoids partially applying the XDP program change on restart failure.

grouping_result.intent: Rollback the XDP program pointer if device reopen fails during setup so XDP updates are not left partially applied.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by restoring the previous XDP program state when mtk_open() fails, preventing the incorrect eth->prog pointer/refcount state left by a partially applied setup.

candidates.rationale: This line commits the new XDP program pointer into eth->prog before the reopen attempt succeeds. If mtk_open(dev) later fails, the driver state is left partially updated, which is the core rollback bug.

This releases the old program immediately after replacement, before confirming that mtk_open(dev) succeeds. On reopen failure, rollback cannot restore correct pointer/refcount state because the old program has already been put.
This returns the reopen result without any rollback path. If mtk_open(dev) fails, the earlier replacement and old program release remain in effect, leaving eth->prog in an inconsistent state.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement installs the new XDP program into eth->prog before the reopen operation is known to succeed. When mtk_open(dev) later fails, the driver has already committed the new pointer, which is the core state-corruption/rollback bug described in the root cause.

This statement drops the reference to the previous XDP program immediately after replacing eth->prog, before setup is complete. If mtk_open(dev) fails afterward, rollback cannot safely restore the old program pointer/refcount state because the old program has already been released.

This statement returns the reopen result directly without any rollback path. On mtk_open(dev) failure, the earlier pointer replacement and old-program put remain in effect, leaving the driver with an incorrect XDP program pointer and refcount state.
